title: Bunny Companion local protocol envelope
description: The request and response envelope carried over the private local socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bunny-companion/runtime.sock. One newline-terminated JSON object each way, at most 65536 bytes in and 4194304 bytes out. The operation must be one of the names below: there is no generic filesystem, command, provider or attribute operation, and a request naming anything else is refused before the runtime is reached. Nothing here is deserialised into a Python object by name, no pickle is used, and no field is ever passed to a shell. A peer declaring a different schemaVersion is refused rather than served with a guess; there is no negotiation and no downgrade path, because both halves of this protocol come from the same build.

requestId.description: Echoed in the answer. A reply whose requestId does not match is discarded by the client, so a confused or replayed response cannot be read as an answer to something else.

params.description: Per-operation, and validated strictly: a parameter the operation does not declare is refused rather than ignored. An ignored parameter is one the caller believes took effect.

transportToken.description: Required only on the loopback-TCP developer fallback used where the platform has no AF_UNIX. Compared in constant time. Absent on the Unix-socket transport that ships, where the peer's user id is checked instead.

error.description: Present when ok is false. The message is one bounded sentence; there is no stack trace on the wire, because a trace is a map of the runtime's internals handed to whatever asked for it.
